stem: Flipper of whale is ____________ type of evidence of evolution.
solution: **(B)** Anatomical. The human hand, foreleg of ox, flipper of whale and patagium of bat look different and do different jobs, but the bones and joints in them have a similar structure. This similarity of internal structure shows a common ancestor, so the flipper of whale is an anatomical evidence of evolution.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: In humans, ____________ chromosome is responsible for maleness.
solution: **(B)** Y. Men have XY sex-chromosomes and women have XX. The X-chromosome is present in both men and women, but the Y-chromosome is present in men only. If the sperm carrying the Y-chromosome fertilises the ovum, the child is a boy, so the Y chromosome is responsible for maleness.

stem: Harmful bacteria like ____________ in the intestine are destroyed due to probiotics.
solution: **(B)** Clostridium. Probiotics contain active useful bacteria such as Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium. They maintain the balance of intestinal microbes by increasing the microbes that help digestion and decreasing the population of harmful microbes such as Clostridium. Lactobacillus is itself a probiotic bacterium, not a harmful one.

stem: Laughter Club is remedy to drive away ____________ .
solution: **(D)** Mental stress. In a laughter club people meet and laugh together freely. Laughing relaxes the mind, diverts it from negative thoughts and keeps a person happy, so a laughter club is a remedy to drive away mental stress.

stem: Srishailam in Andhra Pradesh has ____________ energy power plant.
solution: **(A)** Hydroelectric. Srishailam in Andhra Pradesh is one of the major hydroelectric power plants of India, with a capacity of 1670 MW, along with Tehri (Uttarakhand), Koyana (Maharashtra) and Nathpa Jhakri (Himachal Pradesh).

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Select odd man out: Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Meiosis
solution: Meiosis. Prophase, metaphase and anaphase are stages (phases) of cell division, while meiosis is itself a type of cell division.

stem: Reorganize the following food chain: Grasshopper — Snake — Paddy field — Eagle — Frog
solution: Paddy field \(\rightarrow\) Grasshopper \(\rightarrow\) Frog \(\rightarrow\) Snake \(\rightarrow\) Eagle. The paddy plants are the producers, the grasshopper eats paddy, the frog eats the grasshopper, the snake eats the frog and the eagle eats the snake.

stem: Complete the following correlation: Interferon : Viral infection : : Erythropoietin : ____________
solution: Erythropoietin : Anaemia. Interferon produced by biotechnology is used to treat viral infections, and erythropoietin is used to treat anaemia.

stem: Write the correct word in the box. (Concept map: 'Nature and scope of disaster' branches into three boxes: ____________, Transitional Phase, Reconstruction Phase.)
solution: Phase of emergency (Emergency phase). Considering the nature and scope of disaster, the three phases important for common citizens are the Emergency phase, the Transitional phase and the Reconstruction phase.

stem: Give scientific reason: Peripatus is connecting link between Annelida and Arthropoda.
solution: Peripatus shows characters of annelids such as a segmented body, a thin cuticle and parapodia-like organs. At the same time it shows characters of arthropods such as tracheal respiration and an open circulatory system. Since it has characters of both groups, Peripatus is a connecting link between Annelida and Arthropoda.

stem: Give scientific reason: Our body irritates if it comes in contact with jelly fish.
solution: Jelly fish belongs to phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria). Its tentacles around the mouth bear cnidoblasts (stinging cells), which inject a toxin into the body of the prey and also protect the animal. When our skin touches the tentacles, the cnidoblasts inject this toxin into the skin, so the body irritates.

stem: Give scientific reason: Microbial enzymes are used instead of chemical catalysts in chemical industry.
solution: Microbial enzymes are active at low temperature, pH and pressure, so energy is saved and corrosion-proof instruments are not needed. Enzymes carry out specific reactions, so unwanted by-products are not formed and the cost of purification is reduced. The enzymes can be reused and they avoid waste, so they are eco-friendly. Hence microbial enzymes are used instead of chemical catalysts in chemical industry.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Distinguish between Aerobic respiration and Anaerobic respiration.
solution:
| Aerobic respiration | Anaerobic respiration |
|---|---|
| Oxygen is used. | Oxygen is not used. |
| Glucose is completely oxidised. | Glucose is incompletely oxidised. |
| It occurs in three steps: glycolysis, Krebs cycle and electron transfer chain. | It occurs in two steps: glycolysis and fermentation. |
| It occurs in the cytoplasm and mitochondria. | It occurs in the cytoplasm only. |
| End products are \(CO_2\), \(H_2O\) and a large amount of energy (38 ATP per glucose). | End products are alcohol or organic acids (such as lactic acid) and a small amount of energy. |

stem: Write any two objectives of disaster management.
solution: Objectives of disaster management: (1) Saving human life during the calamity and releasing the people trapped in it. (2) Supplying essential commodities to the people to reduce the effect of the disaster. Rehabilitating the disaster victims and taking protective measures so that the intensity of future disasters is reduced are further objectives.

stem: Give two commercial applications of Biotechnology.
solution: (1) Crop biotechnology: hybrid seeds and genetically modified crops such as Bt cotton, Bt brinjal and Golden rice are developed to increase yield and give resistance to pests, diseases and drought. (2) Human health: vaccines and hormones such as insulin, and interferon for viral infections, are produced on a large scale by biotechnology. Animal husbandry is another field where biotechnology is used commercially.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Explain the process of glycolysis.
solution: Glycolysis is the first step of cellular respiration and takes place in the cytoplasm of the cell. In this process one molecule of glucose is oxidised step by step. At the end of glycolysis, two molecules each of pyruvic acid, ATP, \(NADH_2\) and water are formed. Glycolysis is common to both aerobic and anaerobic respiration: in aerobic respiration the pyruvic acid is converted into acetyl-coenzyme A, which enters the Krebs cycle, and in anaerobic respiration it is converted into alcohol or organic acids by fermentation. Glycolysis was discovered by Embden, Meyerhof and Parnas, so it is also called the EMP pathway.

stem: Write a short note on environmental conservation.
solution: Pollution of air, water and soil, deforestation and the indiscriminate use of natural resources have disturbed the balance of nature. Environmental conservation is needed to maintain this balance and to solve these natural and artificial problems, because we have got the Earth on lease from our future generations. Conservation is possible only when it becomes a public movement, so values like a positive attitude and affection towards nature should be developed in children through education. The government has made laws such as the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 and the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and the National Green Tribunal (2010) enforces them. People's movements such as the Chipko movement also help in conserving the environment.

stem: Write any three distinguishing characters of phylum Echinodermata.
solution: (1) Calcareous spines are present on the body, hence the name echinoderms; the skeleton is made of calcareous spines and/or ossicles. (2) They are found only in the sea; the body is triploblastic and eucoelomate, radially symmetrical in the adult and bilaterally symmetrical in the larva. (3) They move with the help of tube-feet, which also help in capturing prey, and they have a good ability of regeneration. Examples: star fish, sea urchin, brittle star, sea cucumber.

solution: Solid fuels: dung and crop residue (coal is another solid fuel). Liquid fuels: vegetable oils and alcohol (ethanol).

stem: What is meant by stem cells? Write any two uses of stem cells.
solution: Stem cells are special, undifferentiated cells present in the body of multicellular organisms that can divide and give rise to all other types of cells of the body. They are present in the embryo (blastocyst), umbilical cord blood, red bone marrow and adipose tissue. Uses: (1) Regenerative (cell) therapy: stem cells replace dead cells in conditions like diabetes, myocardial infarction, Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease, and produce blood cells needed in anaemia, thalassemia and leukaemia. (2) Organ transplantation: organs like the kidney and liver can be produced from stem cells and transplanted when the original organ fails.

stem: What will you do in the following situation? Why? Child of your neighbour is addicted to tobacco chewing.
solution: What I will do: I will tell the child's parents about the addiction. With them I will talk to the child calmly, explain that tobacco causes cancer of the mouth and lungs and damages the nervous system and heart, and encourage the child to spend free time on sports and hobbies. If needed, we will take the child to a doctor or counsellor or to an organisation working for a tobacco-free society. Why: Children often start tobacco under peer pressure or by imitating elders, and the addiction harms health permanently. Early help can free the child from the addiction before it becomes serious.

stem: Following are some pictures of disasters. Which precautions would you take during these disasters? (A) Earthquake (B) Fire (C) Snake bite
solution: (A) Earthquake: Take shelter under a strong table or bed, or stand near a strong inner wall, and keep away from windows, glass and heavy objects. If outdoors, move to an open ground away from buildings, trees and electric wires; do not use the lift. (B) Fire: Leave the area quickly, moving away from the fire and the direction of the wind, cover the nose and mouth with a wet cloth and keep low to avoid smoke. Inform the fire brigade at once and do not go back for belongings. (C) Snake bite: Keep the victim calm and still and do not let the victim walk. Keep the bitten limb still and below the level of the heart, wash the wound, and do not cut or suck it. Take the victim to the hospital immediately for anti-snake venom.
figureNote: Three disaster pictures on p-02: (A) cracked buildings and split road (earthquake), (B) houses and trees on fire on a hillside (fire / forest fire), (C) a snake biting a foot in a sandal (snake bite).

context: Draw the flow chart showing step by step energy transformation in the following power plants.
stem: Thermal Power Plant
solution: Thermal power plant: Chemical energy in coal \(\rightarrow\) Thermal energy \(\rightarrow\) Kinetic energy in steam \(\rightarrow\) Kinetic energy in turbine \(\rightarrow\) Electrical energy. Coal burns in the boiler and its heat turns water into high-pressure steam, the steam rotates the turbine, and the turbine drives the generator.

context: Draw the flow chart showing step by step energy transformation in the following power plants.
stem: Nuclear Power Plant
solution: Nuclear power plant: Nuclear energy \(\rightarrow\) Thermal energy \(\rightarrow\) Kinetic energy in steam \(\rightarrow\) Kinetic energy in turbine \(\rightarrow\) Electrical energy. Fission of uranium or plutonium nuclei in the reactor releases heat, which produces high-pressure steam to rotate the turbine and the generator.

context: Draw the flow chart showing step by step energy transformation in the following power plants.
stem: Solar Power Plant.
solution: Solar thermal power plant: Solar energy \(\rightarrow\) Thermal energy (in the absorber) \(\rightarrow\) Kinetic energy in steam \(\rightarrow\) Kinetic energy in turbine \(\rightarrow\) Electrical energy. Reflectors concentrate sunlight on absorbers, the heat produces steam, and the steam drives the turbine and generator. In a solar photovoltaic plant the steps are fewer: Solar (light) energy \(\rightarrow\) Electrical energy (DC) in solar cells, which an inverter converts to AC for the grid.
